root_cause.text: The SRCU struct initialized in hci_alloc_dev() is never cleaned up when a Bluetooth HCI device is freed before being fully registered (i.e., before hci_register_dev() sets HCI_UNREGISTER flag), because bt_host_release()’s fallback path only calls kfree() and omits cleanup_srcu_struct().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cleanup_srcu_struct(&hdev->srcu);` in the `else` branch of `bt_host_release()` (the unregistered case) before `kfree(hdev)`, fixing the leak of percpu memory that occurred when early initialization failures bypassed `hci_release_dev()`. The CVE description explicitly states that early failures in HCI UART configuration lead to this scenario.
